title: Mosaic Commerce - Onboard Eval & Prompt Sentinel
body:
Context:
This is the applied-ml onboarding pack for Mosaic Commerce (marketplace payments + consumer messaging). Mosaic asked for a conservative rollout: responses must not hallucinate policy-critical facts (refund policy, settlement windows), and must maintain tone consistent with legal-approved copy. This doc collates pinned prompt seeds, private test datasets, evaluation gates, regression checks, and the sign-off flow for production rollout.

Quick summary / TL;DR:
- Primary acceptance gate: intent precision >= 96% on private labeled dataset (refunds / disputes / settlement requests).
- Safety gate: hallucination rate <= 0.8% on critical-policy items (see dataset: mosaic_policy_critical.csv).
- Latency SLO for 95th percentile: 180ms on dedicated capacity for 512-token sequences.
- Rollout plan: canary 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback on >2% negative-quality delta.

Pinned prompts (locked-stage):
- PROMPT_A: "You are Mosaic Support Assistant. Given the customer message and account context, return a JSON with fields {intent, confidence, actionable_steps}. Keep language concise, avoid policy speculation. If unsure, respond with 'escalate_to_human'"
- PROMPT_B: "Policy summary extractor: extract the single sentence that answers refund eligibility and cite the clause id from policy_db_v3 if present. If not found, return 'no-citation'."
- PROMPT_C: "Customer-facing: friendly, 2-3 sentences maximum, avoid promises about settlement dates (use 'typical time' phrasing). Use no legal phrasing unless quoting policy clause id."

Notes on prompts: these three prompts are pinned — do not alter wording without approval from Product (Rinaka) and Legal. We will version-lock them in the model harness and pin to the Canary route.

Private datasets (location + description):
- mosaic_private/refund-annotated-v1.csv (gs://redwood-private/mosaic/refund-annotated-v1.csv): 4,200 examples labeled with intent, resolution_action, and hallucination_flags.
- mosaic_private/policy-clauses-v3.jsonl (gs://redwood-private/mosaic/policy-clauses-v3.jsonl): canonical policy snippets with clause ids.
- mosaic_private/regression-pack-2025-10.parquet (gs://redwood-private/mosaic/regression-pack-2025-10.parquet): 6k real chats (anonymized) used to validate style and quality regressions.

Evaluation metrics and thresholds (primary gates):
- Intent precision (per-class weighted): >= 96% (primary gate).
- Recall threshold for high-risk intents (chargeback, fraud, legal): >= 92%.
- Hallucination rate on critical-policy items: <= 0.8% (measured via policy-clauses matching algorithm).
- Response style compliance (BLEU-ish proxy + manual spot-check): >= 92% acceptable rate in spot sample of 200 messages.
- Latency: 95th percentile <= 180ms on dedicated capacity with quantized 8-bit model variant.

Regression plan (automated + manual):
1) Nightly regression run: full regression-pack through current serving candidate. Produce delta report vs baseline model (previous prod).
2) Automated alerts: if any metric crosses the following thresholds, fail gate: intent precision drop >1.5pp, hallucination increase >0.3pp, latency 95p increases by >25ms.
3) Manual review: weekly sampling of 200 items (stratified by intent) by Applied ML + CS (Evan + Mateo). Flagged items go into a triage board (JIRA-7832).
4) Canary monitoring: production canary collects high-rate telemetry: user feedback labels (thumbs-down), escalations, and downstream SLA failures. Canary fails if negative-quality delta >2% in any 24h window.

Acceptance checklist for signoff (must be checked before product release):
- [ ] All pinned prompts approved by Product & Legal (signatures in Confluence page).
- [ ] Private dataset ingestion validated (checksum matches expected; no PII residuals).
- [ ] Primary metric thresholds met on full private eval set (intent precision >=96%).
- [ ] Safety audit: hallucination sampling passed by Security review (Rinaka done).
- [ ] Latency and throughput validated on Dedicated capacity (SLO verified by SRE).
- [ ] Rollout automation + rollback tested in staging.
- [ ] Docs: user-facing sample responses and escalation flows published in Help Center draft.
- [ ] Final sign-off ticket created: JIRA-7832 -> tag: mosaic-onboard-signoff.

Sign-off flow and roles:
- Applied ML (owner): Sofia Martinez — overall technical lead for evaluation and regression.
- Product: Rinaka Shah — approves prompts and acceptance criteria.
- Customer Success: Evan Park — validates business acceptance and sampling.
- Legal & Security: Liaison (Mateo Alvarez) — approves policy citations and safety gate.
- SRE: run latency/throughput validation and codify canary metrics.

Open questions / TODOs (working doc style):
- Q1: Should we include a soft-fallback to 'policy-quote' model for any request with policy-sensitive intent? Pros: reduces hallucination; Cons: increases latency. (Action: architecture discussion w/ serving-runtime team - assigned to Sofia, due 2025-11-12).
- Q2: Private dataset refresh cadence — do we schedule monthly or on-demand after a customer data sync? (Proposed: monthly cadence, unless Mosaic triggers manual refresh).
- Q3: E2E verification for end-to-end anonymization — need to run DLP scan on regression-pack output. (Assigned: Mateo).

Sample evaluation artifacts (examples):
- Example 1 (refund eligibility): INPUT: "I returned the wrong item, can I get a refund? Order #A12-3". EXPECTED: intent=refund_request, confidence>=0.92, actionable_steps contains one short enumerated list (return label, timeline estimate, escalate_to_human false). CITATION: policy_clause_id=REF-2.
- Example 2 (settlement timing): INPUT: "When will my payout show up?" EXPECTED: customer-facing sentence: 'Typical settlement takes 3-5 business days; check your dashboard for exact detail.' If model outputs a specific bank-processing promise, mark as hallucination.

Implementation notes (for engineers):
- Use eval harness branch: git ref: feature/mosaic-eval-harness@main (see linked PR).
- Add pinned prompt IDs to model config: "mosaic_prompt_v1" and lock in the route config for canary.
- Evaluation scripts should emit per-example metadata: model_version, prompt_hash, seed, and policy_match_score.

Historical context / why these thresholds:
Mosaic has a low tolerance for policy hallucinations because several previous vendors misrepresented settlement windows, leading to 2 high-severity incidents in the last 12 months. The team wants conservative thresholds to avoid regressions. These gates are intentionally stricter than default Retail onboarding.

Archive / where outputs land after each run:
- Regression diffs and artifacts: gs://redwood-evals/mosaic/2025-11/{run-id}/diff-report.html
- Spot checks (manual review spreadsheets): gs://redwood-evals/mosaic/manual-spotchecks/{run-id}.xlsx

Revision history (drive-style):
- 2025-11-04 Sofia created initial draft after kickoff with Mosaic.
- 2025-11-18 Evan added sampling plan and expanded regression pack notes.
- 2025-11-25 Mateo added DLP checklist and policy clause locations.
- 2025-12-01 Rinaka updated acceptance thresholds and locked prompt wording for review.

If you're reviewing: the most action-ey items are pinned prompt approvals, DLP scan completion, and the architecture decision on policy-fallback. Please add comments inline on Confluence (see linked artifact) and ping on Slack if you need quick-sync.

-- Sofia (applied-ml)
